chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Salma, the servant of the children of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I was with Abu Abdillah عليه السلام when death approached him, and he lost consciousness.

When he regained consciousness, he said: "Give al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn," and he was al-Aftas, "seventy dinars." I said: "Would you give to a man who attacked you with a blade?" He said: "Woe to you! Do you not read the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious:"
And those who join that which Allah has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread the evil reckoning.

key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an; cited as the authority for the Imam’s action
key_terms.الْوَفَاةُ: death; the final illness and passing being described
key_terms.بِالشَّفْرَةِ: with a blade; indicating a prior violent attack
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ دِينَارًا: seventy dinars; the monetary bequest ordered by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ: the evil reckoning; the fearful outcome of divine account
key_terms.يَصِلُونَ: they maintain and join; referring here to keeping ties that Allah commands be upheld

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام give money to a relative who had attacked him?
ai.summary: This narration shows Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام upholding ties of kinship even at the time of death, including toward someone who had previously shown hostility toward him. By citing the Qur'anic verse, the Imam عليه السلام grounds this conduct in Allah’s command to maintain what must be joined and to fear the reckoning.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5551 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid from Salma, the servant of the children of Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"I was with Abu Abdullah (as), when death approached Him (as), and he fell unconscious.
When He (as) regained consciousness, He (as) said:
"Give Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn (who was known as Al-Aftas) 'seventy dinars.'"
I said: "Will you give to a man who once raised a blade against you?"
Imam (as) replied: "Woe to you! Do you not read the Qur'an?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam (as) said: "Have you not heard the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious:
'And those who join that which Allah (swt) has commanded to be joined and fear their Lord (azj) and dread the terrible reckoning'"
(Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:21).
